The alphorn is a traditional lip-vibrated aerophone of the Swiss Alps in Europe, a member of the horn and brass family, Hornbostel–Sachs 423.121.12 / 423.121.22. It is made of wood, traditionally pine and nowadays mostly spruce, about 3 to 4 metres long, with a conical tube bent into a bell at the end and a cup-shaped mouthpiece. The tube has no sideholes, keys or reed; the player produces natural harmonics by lip vibration and air pressure. In the past herdsmen used it to call livestock in the mountains, pass messages and gather scattered cattle, and it later turned to musical and tourist uses.
阿爾卑斯長號源自阿爾卑斯山區牧人工具，學者咸信與利圖斯號相關；約1400年已有類: The alphorn descends from the tools of Alpine herdsmen, and scholars believe it is related to the lituus; a similar instrument existed by about 1400, and it first appears in a German document in 1527. Similar horns are found elsewhere in the European mountains; from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century they were used to send signals between valleys and to call livestock, and players already appear in a stained-glass painting of the late sixteenth century. When dairying moved to villages and towns in the nineteenth century the practical occasion for the instrument declined; in the 1820s the Bernese official Niklaus von Mülinen pushed for its preservation, turning it into a purely musical instrument and a Swiss emblem.
阿爾卑斯長號為唇振氣鳴樂器，圓錐木管與杯形吹口使聲音來自自然泛音列。管身無側孔、: The alphorn is a lip-vibrated aerophone whose conical wooden tube and cup mouthpiece make the sound come from the harmonic series. With no sideholes, keys or reed it cannot bend the pitch and can only produce harmonics; a skilled player reaches nearly four octaves, harmonics 1 to 16, with the fundamental rarely used. Some harmonics do not match the semitones of Western equal temperament, especially the seventh and the eleventh. The player shapes the tune by the length of the breath and the pressure behind it; the source does not say clearly how volume is controlled. Its sound carries several kilometres, and like the other wooden horns of the European mountains it is a signalling instrument.
